record.context_brief: Descendants of prior solution and vanishing graphs
record.original_question: If the trivializing vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} for the tetrahedral flow in dimension d+1 can be constructed from sunflower descendants, determine whether it is enough to use the union of two classes of dimension-(d+1) descendants: first, descendants of the previously known dimension-d solution X_{gamma_3}^d, and second, descendants of vanishing one-vector micro-graphs defined over R^d.

evidence.quote: If yes, is X⃗ gamma3 d+1 found over the union of (d + 1)-descendants for the underlying solution X⃗ gamma3 d and vanishing 1-vector micro-graphs over R d ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix a dimension d ≥ 3 and consider the Nambu–Poisson bracket on R^{d+1} given by a Jacobian determinant with a Casimir density. Within the Kontsevich graph calculus (where directed graphs on n+k vertices encode (n,k)-tensors built as differential-polynomial expressions in the components of a Poisson structure), let γ_3 denote Kontsevich's tetrahedral graph cocycle, and let Q_{γ_3}^{d+1} be the corresponding bivector flow on the space of Nambu–Poisson brackets in dimension d+1. Suppose that this tetrahedral flow is trivial, i.e. there exists a 1-vector graph X⃗_{γ_3}^{d+1} (a "trivializing vector field") whose Schouten bracket with the Nambu–Poisson bivector reproduces Q_{γ_3}^{d+1}. 

Two ways of generating candidate trivializing vector fields in dimension d+1 from data already available in dimension d are by taking (d+1)-descendants of:
(i) the known dimension-d trivializing vector field X⃗_{γ_3}^d for the tetrahedral flow on Nambu–Poisson brackets in R^d, and
(ii) vanishing 1-vector "micro-graphs" defined over R^d (1-vector graphs whose value as a differential operator on R^d is identically zero).

Question. Assuming X⃗_{γ_3}^{d+1} can be expressed as a linear combination of sunflower-type descendants, can it always be found within the linear span of the union of the two classes of (d+1)-descendants (i) and (ii) above?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open problem in the most recent installment of the "Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets" series (a paper devoted to open problems, dated late 2025). No subsequent work resolving this descendant-coverage question for the tetrahedral flow's trivializing vector field in dimension d+1 was found.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu-Poisson brackets, VI. Open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Paper dedicated to open problems concerning Kontsevich's tetrahedral graph cocycle action on Nambu–Poisson brackets and the trivializing vector fields built from graph descendants.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open problem in this 2025 problems-paper.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, II. The tetrahedral flow is a coboundary in 4D
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes that the tetrahedral flow is trivializable in dimension 4, providing the prior dimension-d solution X⃗_{γ_3}^d referenced in the question.
status_evidence.claim: The known lower-dimensional trivializing vector field exists and motivates the descendant-construction question.
